executiveSummary: GM0339's identity, 2025 boundary, one BAG place, two BRT settlement labels, two neighbourhoods and headline CBS controls are coherent, and the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Veiligheidsregio Utrecht explicitly includes Renswoude among the municipalities affected in a major Grebbedijk breach scenario, while the public VNK2 dike-ring scenario describes a staged pathway through Veenendaal and the Slaperdijk before water spreads through the wider Gelderse Vallei. The generic river preset does not select that or another governed event: it already reports 0.484435 m and 288 affected people-equivalent at T+6 and then holds a 1.376237 m legacy flood amplitude from T+12 through T+72 without a breach, hydrograph, defence state, arrival surface, recession or dewatering record. A controlled T+24 wildfire probe placed the ignition inside rural BU03390009, yet non-source urban BU03390000 received the higher local hazard, exposing the common municipality-severity-plus-hash allocation. Renswoude's own rainwater programme documents that the mixed sewer can become very full during extreme rain and that a separate storm-water pipe to nearby surface water is still being delivered street by street; neither that pathway nor terrain, rainfall, sewers, streams or controls governs model depth. Four static road-border records reduce to two physical corridors, A12 and N224. Sixty-two water-register objects, utility territories, one grid-planning sample, antenna and education records, and transport schedules provide useful context but no live connected topology, capacity, outage, backup, incident occupancy or restoration evidence. Exact local consequences and T+72 recovery must be suppressed or clearly retained as synthetic exercise indices until governed event, lifeline and action evidence exists; source nulls and empty or horizon-limited local matches remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0339 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, settlement and safety-region records
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; PDOK/Kadaster generated-source snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026
supports: The official records identify GM0339 as Renswoude in Utrecht and Veiligheidsregio Utrecht. The generated centre [5.5293607868112264, 52.06081120904292] is inside the generalized 2025 boundary, and feature id, bundle code/name, province and safety-region joins agree.

CBS reports 5,782 residents, density 314/km², 16.9% aged 65 or older and 630 one-person households. BU03390000 Renswoude reports 3,605 residents and BU03390009 Verspreide huizen 2,175; the two rounded rows total 5,780, two below the municipality total (-0.035%), and deterministic allocation reconciles them to 3,606 and 2,176 without changing source observations.

The two rows total 2,270 households and 980 rounded age-65-plus residents. All 36 deployed statistic fields cover both rows except district-heating share and public charging points, which are null in both; null, suppression and non-applicability remain NoData rather than zero.

BAG supplies one active place, Renswoude, and BRT supplies two settlement labels: Renswoude as woonkern and Emminkhuizen as buurtschap. BAG place, BRT settlement and CBS neighbourhood are different official feature classes and not duplicate population measures.
The annual resident baseline does not measure event-time workers, visitors, pupils, road users, responders, shelter occupants or people temporarily needing assistance.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel Veiligheidsregio Utrecht 2023
supports: The regional risk profile says a single Grebbedijk breach between Rhenen and Wageningen can have major impact and explicitly names Veenendaal, Rhenen, Renswoude and Amersfoort among affected municipalities, including conditions requiring large-scale evacuation.

The profile treats river flooding, heavy-rain water nuisance, drought/nature fire, storm, ice and prolonged extreme weather as distinct mechanisms. Heavy rain can impair incident accessibility, while wind or ice can cause power failure and prolonged conditions can exhaust resources or leave areas inaccessible.

It identifies electricity/gas, drinking water, ICT/telecom, finance and water management as vital processes and warns that cyber or digital disruption of IT/OT can cascade through critical infrastructure.

A regional risk description establishes relevance and governance context, not a selected local event, probability, breach state, inundation field, outage, capacity, action completion or T+72 forecast.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Projectbureau Veiligheid Nederland in Kaart
evidenceSources.title: E03 — VNK2 dike-ring report 45, Gelderse Vallei, hosted by the Grebbedijk project
evidenceSources.edition: VNK2 dike-ring scenario report; historical scenario evidence, not a current forecast
supports: The report describes dike ring 45 and a Grebbedijk breach pathway: water reaches the edge of Veenendaal after about eight hours, most of Veenendaal after about 20 hours and the Slaperdijk after about 30 hours, after which it spreads farther through the ring.
Its scenario states that most cores in the area, including Renswoude, can be inundated; locally deep water is possible in the wider ring, especially on the upstream side of the Slaperdijk.

This is an older, assumption-bound breach analysis. It is not evidence that the dike is currently failing, that this breach location is active, that its timing applies to another event or that one depth can be assigned uniformly to GM0339.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Afvoer regenwater: local mixed-sewer and separate storm-water works
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal project page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality says the existing mixed sewer can become very full during extreme rainfall and describes adding a separate storm-water pipe that discharges to nearby surface water or a stream.

The programme began with public-space upgrades from 2025; Eikenlaan work was completed in spring 2026, while work at Lijsterbeslaan, Dickerijst and Beukenlaan is stated to begin in 2027. Programme intent and partial delivery are not municipality-wide present drainage capacity.

The page establishes a local rain–street–sewer–surface-water pathway and increasing heavy-rain pressure, but publishes no machine-readable rainfall field, hydraulic surface, sewer/catchment topology, pipe/pump capacity, live state, flood depth or recovery estimate.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe / Grebbedijk project partners
evidenceSources.title: E05 — Current Grebbedijk project and safety lifecycle FAQ
supports: The project FAQ describes the current Grebbedijk as strong enough while also explaining that it does not meet the future standard and is being reinforced. Improvement need or planned work is not evidence of current failure.

The page distinguishes routine monitoring and escalating high-water response, including preparation for failure or evacuation at the highest alert phase. Preparedness guidance is not a live alert or completed evacuation.
Current lifecycle context must accompany use of the older VNK2 scenario so a hypothetical breach is not presented as observed present-day dike condition.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Renswoude heat plan and public-health preparedness
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal heat-plan page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality describes more warm days and identifies older residents, babies, young children and people in poor health as especially vulnerable during heat.

It identifies a drinking-water tap point at Sporthal De Hokhorst and gives protective advice. A named tap or preparedness instruction does not establish activation, throughput, water quality, accessibility, staff, stocks or incident-time cooling capacity.
The page does not provide a gridded forecast, urban heat field, indoor exposure, tree/shade data, care occupancy, mortality function or T+72 outcome.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water-asset, utility-territory, grid-planning, antenna and education context
evidenceSources.edition: Public-context snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; provider and contributor dates vary
supports: Full CBS-boundary containment assigns 62 HWH objects to GM0339: 60 weirs, one surface-water pump and one sewer pump. All register statuses are 'gerealiseerd', but only one object has a non-null capacity; registration does not prove connected catchment, current operation, power, control, reserve, backup or restoration.

Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting centre-point lookups identify Stedin for electricity and gas, Vitens for water and Ziggo for media, while the drainage lookup is empty. Territory at one reference point is not complete municipal topology, service availability, pressure/quality, outage or restoration.

The single NBNL sample at postcode 3927CK is assigned to service area CM38 Veenendaal. It reports large-user planning values and queues for withdrawal and injection, 28 projects and earliest project year 2030; it is not a municipal total, live load, reserve margin, outage, topology or completion record.

RDI assigns seven antenna sites with 18 installations, including five mobile and two fixed-link sites, and DUO supplies four education locations. Neither point inventory establishes radio coverage/backhaul/power/backup, shelter designation, occupancy, staff, supplies or care capacity.

HWH carries CC BY-SA 4.0 and contributor-coverage caveats; Mijn Aansluiting is Public Domain. No exact standard licence identifier was found for the deployed NBNL planning extract or RDI WFS, so downstream reuse must preserve the source-specific uncertainty.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / KNMI / NDW / RIVM / Provincie Utrecht
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Static transport and bounded current-context deployment for GM0339
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail, GTFS and current-context snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB generates four border records: A12 links to Utrechtse Heuvelrug and Veenendaal and N224 links to Ede and Scherpenzeel. The paired A12 records share physical corridor NWB-road-12 and the paired N224 records share NWB-road-224, so boundary ends are never additive independent throughput.

The graph treats roads as Mobility and assumed road-logistics Supply context only. Geometry and generalized scenario capacities do not establish lanes, direction, congestion, damage, inspection, closure, emergency priority, reroute or event-time throughput.

The bounded ProRail station layer assigns no station to GM0339, while the best-effort OVapi GTFS snapshot spatially assigns 11 stop areas. Static geometry and timetables do not prove vehicles running, passenger or evacuation capacity, accessibility or restoration.

The deployment assigns no local KNMI fixed weather station or recent seismic origin, RIVM PM2.5 station or acute-care location, RWS Waterinfo observation/forecast, government-service location or NDW road situation. One province-wide warning record is level 0 in the retrieval snapshot. Empty spatial/time matches and a transient level are NoData/current context, not proof of no hazard, normal future weather, open roads, local care access or safety.

identity.summary: GM0339, Renswoude, Utrecht and Veiligheidsregio Utrecht agree across official and generated 2025 records.
notes: Feature id, bundle code/name, province, safety region and 2025 boundary/statistics editions agree.
The generated municipality centre is inside the generalized boundary, and the one active BAG place is Renswoude.
No identity, province, safety-region or headline-population contradiction was found.

geography.summary: Administrative containment is coherent but cannot resolve Grebbedijk pathways, Slaperdijk compartmentation, local streams, sewers or lifelines.
notes: A generalized municipality polygon and two neighbourhoods are not hydraulic cells, defence sections, arrival-time zones, sewer catchments, heat surfaces, fuel areas or utility service areas.

The official breach scenario is staged through Veenendaal and the Slaperdijk before wider spread; it cannot be represented by one GM0339 scalar without its event assumptions and full-resolution geometry.
BAG/BRT centres and labels aid orientation but do not prove hazard containment, incident population, access, evacuation priority or service state.

demography.summary: Municipal and neighbourhood resident controls reconcile within CBS rounding, with important incident-occupancy limits.
notes: CBS reports 5,782 residents; the two neighbourhood rows total 5,780 (-2, -0.035%), consistent with rounded source cells.
The neighbourhood rows total 2,270 households and 980 rounded age-65-plus residents; the headline share is 16.9% and one-person households total 630.
Deterministic allocation reconciles the two rows to 3,606 and 2,176 for model arithmetic without presenting allocated values as source observations.
Annual residence data omit workers, visitors, pupils, road users, responders, shelter occupancy and event-time support needs.

regionalDetail.summary: The two neighbourhood rows are unusually complete, but two indicator families and infrastructure context remain missing or non-causal.
notes: District-heating share and public charging are null in both neighbourhoods; all other deployed statistic fields cover 2/2 rows.
The municipality documents an incompletely delivered separate storm-water programme, but publishes no municipality-wide sewer/hydraulic topology or live control state.

Water objects, providers, grid planning, antennas and education points retain coverage, licence and evidence-class limitations; counts or register status never prove connectivity, comparable capacity, present operation or recovery.

settlements.summary: One BAG place and two BRT settlement labels are contained and semantically coherent for Renswoude.
notes: The active BAG place is Renswoude; BRT identifies Renswoude as woonkern and Emminkhuizen as buurtschap.
BAG place, BRT settlement and CBS neighbourhood are distinct feature classes and must not be used as duplicate population totals.
Neither settlement type establishes incident occupancy, shelter role, road access, hazard footprint or service territory.

transport.summary: A12 and N224 boundary identities are coherent, but duplicated corridor ends and static transit do not establish operational access.
notes: Four border records reduce to two physical corridors: A12 toward Utrechtse Heuvelrug/Veenendaal and N224 toward Ede/Scherpenzeel. Same-corridor ends are not independent additive routes.
No ProRail station is assigned locally; 11 spatial GTFS stop areas are timetable/context records without live vehicles, accessibility or capacity.

VRU notes that water nuisance and prolonged weather can impair accessibility. The graph has no time-valid closure, inspection, congestion, emergency-priority or reroute state, and an empty NDW match never proves open.

emergencyContext.summary: Official risks, plans and public registers support preparedness context but not a live GM0339 incident picture or resource state.
notes: The Grebbedijk scenario, regional risk profile, rainwater programme and heat plan establish locally relevant mechanisms and vulnerable groups but no active warning, selected event, completed action or forecast through T+72.
No local acute-care record was assigned; that indicates dependence on external care locations and route/acceptance evidence, not absence of care access.

Water assets, provider territories, one grid-planning sample, antennas, schools, roads and stops do not supply emergency staffing, occupancy, backup, stock, priority, crew, command or restoration status.
Every current-context absence or stale/limited snapshot remains Unknown/NoData, never an all-clear.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All required presets, checkpoints and services execute deterministically for GM0339.
notes: Focused municipality gate covered 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services and passed 2/2 tests in the initial 32.18-second run.

The suite checks finite bounded outputs, exact municipality/local reconciliation, identical repeated T+24 runs, preset alignment, route-proxy semantics, neutral official regions and no synthetic hubs.
Execution coverage establishes software behavior, not authoritative local calibration or incident truth.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, accounting ledgers, deterministic replay and monotonic burden contracts pass.
notes: Availability remains in [0,1]; hazard contributions, service-stage deltas, weighted pressure, local demand/delivery and population allocation reconcile within test tolerance.
Event-attributable deprived person-hours are monotonic and zero-intensity controls remain bounded.
Arithmetic closure is internal consistency only; it does not validate event selection, local spatial allocation, network causality or recovery operations.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A municipality scalar plus common hashed local allocation cannot reproduce staged flood arrival or source-specific neighbourhood exposure.
notes: The river preset reports 0.484435 m and 288 affected people-equivalent at T+6, reaches a 1.376237 m legacy flood amplitude by T+12 and retains it through T+72 without selecting a breach, hydrograph, defence state or arrival surface. It therefore cannot be attributed to the VNK2 pathway, which reaches Veenendaal's edge around eight hours and the Slaperdijk around 30 hours before wider spread.

The local model derives each neighbourhood hazard from municipality severity multiplied by a fixed region hash; all presets reuse that ordering whenever their scalar is active, despite water, wind, heat, ice, fire/smoke, earthquake and cyber having different spatial mechanisms.

In a controlled T+24 wildfire probe with the epicentre placed inside rural BU03390009, non-source BU03390000 received hazard 0.571857 while source-containing BU03390009 received 0.561210. The source point did not govern local exposure.

Canonical wildfire has zero direct local flame but synthetic smoke, coastal has zero direct flood, and earthquake has no T+24 ground motion. Those zero components are bounded exercise results, not local all-clears.

serviceDependencies.summary: Eight service balances calculate, but physical water, utility, telecom, care, transport and supply dependencies are absent.
notes: At compound T+24 the model reports power 0.318146, water 0.387320, drainage 0.272752, gas 0.581311, telecom 0.174421, mobility 0.889703, facilities 0.532953 and supply 0.730862; no local operator validates these exact fractions.

The 62 HWH points, Stedin/Vitens/Ziggo territories, CM38 planning sample, antenna/education points and heat-plan tap are non-causal context. They do not provide connectivity, load/flow, live outage/quality, backup, stock, staffing, priority users, crews or repair time.

NWB routes affect only Mobility and assumed road-logistics Supply. The graph does not encode A12/N224 corridor state, external care access, water-management power/control dependencies or telecom backhaul.
Neighbourhood service variation arises from deterministic service seeds and demographic context rather than validated physical service areas or assets.

causalTrace.summary: Synthetic arithmetic is traceable, but no governed local event, target, network state or intervention supports the exact consequences.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service-stage deltas close to availability, weighted losses close to pressure and local demand/delivery reconcile to municipality totals.
Official plans, scenario reports, static assets, provider territories, routes and current-context records remain evidence context rather than implicit model calibration.

The trace selects no Grebbedijk breach/hydrograph, rainfall field, sewer/stream/control state, heat forecast, ignition/perimeter, earthquake field, cyber target, lifeline topology, incident command or completed action.
A closed synthetic ledger explains computation but cannot establish empirical causation, probability, current failure or decision-grade precision.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 river and compound consequences lack recession, dewatering, inspection, operator restoration and confirmed action evidence.
notes: River severity 0.425096 and legacy depth 1.376237 m persist from T+24 to T+72; affected rises from 2,691 to 2,884, facilities availability falls from 0.518214 to 0.348951 and burden reaches 200,064.36 person-hours without a hydraulic or action ledger.

Compound affected rises from 3,100 at T+24 to 3,364 at T+72 and burden reaches 231,608.73 person-hours; the service trajectory is generated without authority decisions, crews, materials, fuel, route inspection, care diversion, welfare checks or completion evidence.

The public sources provide no selected arrival/recession field, current sewer/pump state, A12/N224 inspection, operator restoration estimate, external-care acceptance or local resource inventory through 72 hours.

Every persistence, deterioration or recovery step needs a typed event/action/resource record with authority, issue/valid time, uncertainty and completion state; 72 hours is a preparedness horizon, not a recovery promise.

findings.summary: Generated identity, safety-region membership, settlements and 2025 demographic controls are coherent.
findings.evidence: GM0339, Renswoude, Utrecht and Veiligheidsregio Utrecht agree; the generated centre is contained. CBS reports 5,782 residents while two rounded neighbourhood rows total 5,780 (-0.035%) and reconcile deterministically without rewriting observations.
findings.action: Retain source edition/retrieval, full-resolution geometry access, publisher-null semantics, published-versus-allocated reconciliation and distinct BAG/BRT/CBS feature semantics on refresh.

findings.summary: Null indicators and empty bounded current-context matches remain explicit Unknown/NoData.
findings.evidence: District heat and charging are null in both neighbourhoods; only one of 62 HWH capacities is non-null and drainage-provider lookup is empty. No local Waterinfo, KNMI fixed weather/seismic, NDW, PM2.5, acute-care or government-service point is assigned; one provincial warning level is only a retrieval-time snapshot.
findings.action: Preserve publisher, version, retrieval/issue/valid time, licence or absent licence, spatial/time coverage, evidence class, NoData mask and reason. Never coerce absence to zero, normal, open, safe, available or persistence.

findings.summary: Generic river output has false local precision and does not instantiate a governed Grebbedijk event.
findings.evidence: The model reports 0.484435 m/288 affected at T+6 and 1.376237 m from T+12 through T+72 without a breach or boundary condition. VRU explicitly says a Grebbedijk breach can affect Renswoude, but VNK2 describes staged arrival through Veenendaal and the Slaperdijk; the current project FAQ describes the dike as strong enough today while being reinforced for the future standard.
findings.action: Suppress decision-facing depth, affected count, percentages and hotspot claims until an authority-approved event binds hydrograph/discharge, defence section and breach/overtopping state, Slaperdijk/Valleikanaal assumptions, full inundation and arrival/recession surfaces, current lifecycle, uncertainty, version/licence and valid time. Missing scenario data remains Unknown, not zero risk.

findings.summary: A shared local hash overrides hazard-source containment and reuses one neighbourhood ordering across mechanisms.
findings.evidence: All presets derive both neighbourhood hazards from municipality severity and the same fixed region hash. In a controlled T+24 wildfire with the ignition inside BU03390009, non-source BU03390000 scored 0.571857 and source-containing BU03390009 0.561210, demonstrating that the source location did not govern local exposure.
findings.action: Remove unsupported local ranks/hotspots and affected allocations until each mechanism has versioned spatial evidence and containment/intersection logic. Add a regression requiring an ignition-containing area to receive source-consistent direct fire exposure or explicit Unknown, and test flood arrival, rain, heat, wind/ice, smoke, ground motion and named cyber targets independently.

findings.summary: Pluvial depth omits Renswoude's mixed sewer, new storm-water pipe, receiving surface water and terrain.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports severity 0.257076, 0.355951 m legacy depth, 537 affected and drainage availability 0.538993. The municipality says its mixed sewer can become very full in extreme rain and is adding a separate pipe to nearby surface water street by street; no rainfall, AHN/soil/groundwater, imperviousness, sewer/catchment, stream level or current pump/control state governs the scalar.
findings.action: Integrate a selected municipal/water-board stress test or hydraulic field with rainfall, terrain/soil/groundwater, imperviousness, sewer/catchments, receiving streams and governed pump/weir state. Carry CRS, unit, native resolution, licence, issue/valid time, uncertainty and NoData; partial works never become blanket present capacity.

findings.summary: Four boundary records overstate independence and lack event-time A12/N224 and external-care state.
findings.evidence: A12 records toward Utrechtse Heuvelrug and Veenendaal share NWB-road-12; N224 records toward Ede and Scherpenzeel share NWB-road-224. Generalized route capacity is a scenario ceiling, not additive throughput. Zero NDW matches and no local rail/acute-care point do not prove routes open or care unavailable.
findings.action: Retain all audited boundary edges but model physical-corridor identity, direction/class, bridge/low-point dependencies, authority, issue/valid time, inspection and open/restricted/closed/Unknown state. Resolve confirmed alternatives and external care/supply destinations without summing corridor ends or inferring operation from silence.

findings.summary: Sixty-two water-chain objects are useful register context but not an operational drainage/hydraulic network.
findings.evidence: HWH assigns 60 weirs, one surface-water pump and one sewer pump; only one capacity is non-null and every object is registered 'gerealiseerd'. The records do not establish connected catchments, unit comparability, control/power/backup, present operation, failure or restoration.
findings.action: Retain each source object, manager/null, raw capacity and unit, register status, collection, retrieval, CC BY-SA licence and coverage caveat. Seek authorized aggregate municipal/water-board topology and state; never sum unlike values or infer operation, reserve or safety.

findings.summary: Exact utility, telecom, facility and supply continuity percentages have no operator or care-chain evidence.
findings.evidence: At compound T+24 the eight availability values range from telecom 0.174421 to mobility 0.889703. Stedin/Vitens/Ziggo territories, CM38 Veenendaal planning, 62 water objects, seven antenna sites, four education locations, a heat-plan tap and static roads/stops provide no connected topology, live load/flow/outage, pressure/quality, backhaul, backup, occupancy, staff, stock, crews or repair estimates.
findings.action: Keep public context affectsSimulation=false and operational values explicitly synthetic/Unknown. Ingest only authorized, time-scoped operator, water-board and care/logistics aggregates; expose dependency and validity without publishing sensitive topology.

findings.summary: No auditable first-72-hour decision, resource or completion ledger drives persistence or recovery.
findings.evidence: River affected rises from 2,691 to 2,884 and compound from 3,100 to 3,364 between T+24 and T+72; facilities worsen substantially and burden reaches 200,064.36 and 231,608.73 person-hours respectively. No warning, dike/control decision, evacuation/reception, route inspection, dewatering, temporary water, care transfer, utility repair, fuel/supply or welfare-check record drives those trajectories.
findings.action: Add Unknown-first records with authority, event, issue/valid time, assigned resource, target, state, confidence and completion evidence. Separate water-board, municipality, VRU, road, utility, telecom, care and logistics responsibilities; only confirmed actions alter recovery.

findings.summary: Storm, heat/drought, winter, cyber, fire/smoke, coastal and earthquake presets remain bounded but locally uncalibrated exercises.
findings.evidence: VRU and the municipal heat plan establish relevance and vulnerable groups, but the model selects no local forecast, wind/ice field, heat surface, cyber target, ignition/perimeter, smoke observation or ground-motion field. Canonical wildfire has zero direct local flame but synthetic smoke, earthquake has no T+24 ground motion and coastal has zero direct depth; none is a local all-clear.
findings.action: Retain these presets only as clearly labelled synthetic exercises. Require a named time-valid observation/forecast, ignition/perimeter, target or event field where appropriate, preserve indirect effects separately and render absent evidence as Unknown.

corrections.summary: Gate GM0339 river consequences behind a selected, versioned hydraulic and defence event.
corrections.validation: River depth, arrival, affected population and service percentages remain Unknown until a source-approved hydrograph/discharge, Grebbedijk section and breach/overtopping state, Slaperdijk/Valleikanaal assumptions, full-resolution inundation/arrival/recession field, current lifecycle, source/version/licence, valid time and uncertainty are present; the VNK2 historical scenario can never imply current dike failure.

corrections.summary: Replace common hashed neighbourhood exposure with hazard-specific spatial fields and source containment.
corrections.validation: A controlled ignition inside BU03390009 produces source-consistent direct fire exposure or explicit Unknown instead of higher exposure in non-source BU03390000; Grebbedijk arrival, local rain/sewer/stream water, heat, wind/ice, smoke, ground motion and named cyber targets use independent versioned geometry and NoData masks.

corrections.summary: Preserve public water, utility, grid, antenna, education and transport records as non-causal context until governed topology/state exists.
corrections.validation: Cards and exports expose publisher, collection/version, retrieval/issue/valid time, licence or absent licence, coverage, evidence class and affectsSimulation=false; points, territories, queues, register status, route ends and empty matches cannot create exact service availability, capacity, outage, operation or safety.

corrections.summary: Model A12/N224 and external care/supply access as typed, non-additive, time-valid dependencies.
corrections.validation: The four border records retain two physical-corridor identities; direction/class and open/restricted/closed/Unknown state require authority plus issue/valid time, route ends are not summed, zero NDW records do not mean open and external care/supply claims require a confirmed destination and passable path.

corrections.summary: Add an Unknown-first first-72-hour incident, action and resource ledger.
corrections.validation: Warnings, monitoring, evacuation/reception, dike/water-control decisions, road inspection, dewatering, temporary water/sanitation, care transfer, utility/telecom repair, fuel/supply and welfare actions show authority, issue/valid time, assignment, resource, confidence and completion; only confirmed actions change T+6 through T+72 recovery.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source supplies a complete safe-to-publish Stedin/Vitens/gas/telecom/wastewater topology, live control state, backup endurance, priority users, crews, inventories or restoration estimate for GM0339.

A defensible Grebbedijk outcome requires event hydrograph/discharge, breach/overtopping and defence state, Slaperdijk/Valleikanaal assumptions, terrain, full inundation and arrival/recession/dewatering fields; the historical VNK2 scenario is not a current forecast or failure report.

Local pluvial outcomes require rainfall, terrain/soil/groundwater, imperviousness, sewer/catchment and receiving-water state; a municipal work programme and 62 register points do not supply that operational model.

Static NWB, ProRail and GTFS omit event-time road, rail and bus operation, inspection, accessibility, congestion, ambulance/freight/evacuation capacity and restoration; empty NDW or station matches prove neither access nor isolation.
CBS/BAG/BRT/DUO omit workers, visitors, pupils present, road users, responders, assisted-evacuation needs, external-care acceptance, shelters and household stocks.
Affected population is a people-equivalent exercise index and deprived person-hours is weighted local service deprivation, not casualties, evacuations, patients or customer interruptions.
Current weather, water, roads, providers, care and utility states can change after completion; stale, empty, horizon-limited or out-of-coverage inputs must degrade to Unknown.
provinceReviewFlags: Coordinate the Grebbedijk/dike-ring 45 event, Slaperdijk and Valleikanaal assumptions, evacuation phases and arrival/recession evidence across Renswoude, Rhenen, Veenendaal, Amersfoort, Utrecht province, Gelderland, VRU, VGGM and Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe.

Join municipal rain/sewer works to water-board catchments and receiving streams without converting project intent, register status or current regional water context into present capacity or an all-clear.

Treat the A12 and N224 as two cross-boundary physical corridors, not four independent routes; coordinate inspection, restriction, alternatives, external acute care and supply access with Utrechtse Heuvelrug, Veenendaal, Ede and Scherpenzeel.
Audit CM38 Veenendaal and Stedin/Vitens/Ziggo/telecom dependencies across municipal borders using privacy-safe operator aggregates and consistent issue/valid times.
Test and remove the common two-neighbourhood rank across Grebbedijk/pluvial water, urban/rural heat, wind/ice, wildfire/smoke and named cyber targets before any province comparison or prioritisation.
